newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UK Virgin says may buy S.Africa's Sun Air.
newsitem.headline: UK Virgin says may buy S.Africa's Sun Air.

text.p: Virgin Atlantic Airways owner Richard Branson said on Thursday that he was interested in buying South African state-owned airline Sun Air to develop it into a "pan-African" low-cost regional carrier.

He said that the local airline would link in with Virgin Atlantic's new service between London and Johannesburg which started on Thursday and would form the base for developing a pan-African network on the model of Branson's new Virgin Express shorthaul airline in Europe.
"It depends what the price is but yes, we would like to look at it (buying Sun Air)," he told a news conference.
"We get on well with the people who run it... and I think it can be developed as a force in Africa," he said.
Last month Virgin announced a new code sharing pact with Sun Air which currently flies between Johannesburg, Durban and Cape Town using a fleet of two Boeing 727s and five McDonnell Douglas DC9s.

But Branson told reporters shortly after Virgin's inaugural London-Johannesburg arrival that he was now interested in taking over Sun Air if the South African government's plans to privatise the airline in March go ahead.
It would then form the basis for developing a Virgin Express in Africa.
A spokesman said that Virgin would be speaking to South African Transport Mininster Mac Maharaj in more detail about his plans later on Thursday.
The spokesman said Virgin believes that Sun Air currently makes a profit of about four million pounds a year.
